summary: catalogai harvests browser credential stores and side-loads Chrome extensions under a cover-story name
details: catalogai 0.1.2 presents itself as a semantic-search / AI-catalog library but the shipped modules perform browser credential theft and remote-controlled Chrome extension installation. catalogai/export.py enumerates Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi, and Chromium user-data directories across all detected profiles, copies extension Local/Sync settings, Local Storage, and the LastPass extension database into a temp directory, zips the result, computes a hardware fingerprint, and uploads the archive via cognikit.fileops.upload_file_to_public_api. catalogai/extensions.py runs get_extinfo(), which shells out to PowerShell (Get-CimInstance Win32_UserAccount) to capture the current user's Windows SID, gathers installed-browser paths and each profile's Secure Preferences JSON, writes extinfo.json, and uploads it to the same sink. extensions.py also exposes handle_install_extension / handle_grab_extension network-message handlers that download extdata.zip, extract it into each Chrome user-data Extensions directory, terminate running Chrome via taskkill, rewrite Secure Preferences, set the HKCU Chrome policy values DeveloperToolsAvailability=0 and ExtensionDeveloperModeSettings=0 to hide developer-mode UI, and relaunch Chrome with --restore-last-session. The package's __init__ is inert, but the runtime dependency cognikit>=0.1.2 supplies the upload_file_to_public_api, send_message, and get_hardware_fingerprint primitives used by the harmful modules.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
